html:
The Maká are a Matacoan people of the Gran Chaco of Paraguay. They once lived along the lower Pilcomayo river, and now live mainly near the Río Negro in Presidente Hayes department and in and around Asunción. About 1,500 speak their language.

Their language is related to that of the Nivaclé and the Wichí. In the Chaco War of 1932 to 1935 between Paraguay and Bolivia, some Maká served as scouts. The Russian émigré general Juan Belaieff, who had explored the Chaco, helped them settle near Asunción afterwards. Today many sell crafts in the city. Their Chaco neighbours include the Enxet.
